Subject: Request: throughput & SLA mapping for Dedicated commitment

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking this on. We're working toward a Dedicated commitment decision and need a clear throughput -> GPU slab mapping plus SLO fit so we can align procurement and engineering. High level constraints:

- Model: customer-hosted variant (we call it "Archie-v2", ~13B FP16-ish equivalent) to be served on Redwood Dedicated.
- Expected baseline: 45 requests/sec average, average generation length ~120 tokens, 20% of requests are streaming; peak 1-hour window up to 220 req/sec.
- P95 latency target for interactive flows: <= 300ms server-side (token latency to first token ideally <200ms).
- Peak concurrency distribution: 70% short (<50 tokens), 25% medium (50–250 tokens), 5% long (>250 tokens).
- Important: we will use prefix caching where possible for repeated prompts.
- Procurement timeline: need draft SOW & capacity model by end of Nov, final by mid-Dec.

I've attached our workload profile CSV with sampled traces. Can you provide: tokens/sec estimates, required reserved slabs for steady-state and peak with headroom, whether quantization or KV cache changes materially reduce required GPUs, and a recommended working reserve / burst policy? Also flag any assumptions you need.

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Hart
Head of Product, Archimedes Labs
emma.hart@archimedeslabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: archimedes_workload_profile.csv (sampled traces; columns: timestamp, req_id, tokens_out, streaming_flag)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hart <emma.hart@archimedeslabs.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: throughput & SLA mapping for Dedicated commitment

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the profile, this is enough to produce a data-backed capacity snapshot. High-level takeaways up front, then a short model and assumptions:

Executive summary (quick):
- Steady-state reserved: 6 dedicated GPU slabs (H200-equivalent) gives ~320k tokens/min sustained (~5.3k tokens/sec) with KV prefix cache assumed 45% hit rate; fits your baseline and leaves ~35% headroom for normal diurnal swings.
- Peak hour (burst): allow 2x burst capacity (12 slabs) with our burst routing — will keep P95 <= ~280ms for short/medium requests if caching and batching are enabled.
- Quantization to 4-bit (llm-int8/4) reduces steady slab needs by ~20% in our perf tests; combined with caching this could drop steady reserve to ~5 slabs.

Model & assumptions:
- Model perf: we used internal profile for a 13B-class decoder with typical Redwood kernels: median token generation latency per GPU under single-request low-batch = 12ms/token; at practical batching (batch sizes 8–16) effective throughput per slab = ~45k tokens/sec (H200-equivalent).
- KV cache: we assumed 45% cache hit on prefixes for your corpus sample; cache hits avoid full attention compute and reduce token cost by ~2.3x for those requests; please confirm if your trace is representative.
- Batching: smart continuous batching expected to increase GPU throughput by ~1.6x vs naive single-request paths during medium loads.
- Safety margin/headroom: we modeled headroom as 35% for steady-state (to allow one abnormal hour) and 60% for burst capacity planning.

Sizing math (rounded):
- Baseline tokens/sec estimate from traces (w/o caching): ~3.9k tps. With 45% cache hit and batching -> effective token demand on compute ~2.2k tps.
- Effective throughput per slab (with batching + quantization off) ~800 tps per slab. => 3 slabs would cover compute demand, but we recommend 6 slabs for redundancy, headroom, and maintenance windows.
- If you enable 4-bit quantization we estimate per-slab throughput restores to ~1,000 tps -> steady reserve could be 5 slabs.

SLO fit notes:
- With 6 slabs, active caching, and continuous batching, we project p95 server-side generation latency ~250–290ms depending on prompt length mix; short requests are comfortably under 200ms.
- Tail risk: long-tail >500ms primarily driven by large generations & cold KV misses. We recommend fallback policy: route long offline generations to a non-interactive tier or increase burst pool for those cases.

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Confirm that the trace's 45% cache-hit assumption looks right or send a cleaned sample focusing on repeat prompt fingerprints.
2) Confirm target for quantization — if you require FP16 for quality we will model without quant; otherwise we can quantify quality/regression trade-offs.
3) Confirm whether you want a reserved burst pool included in the initial quote (we can price steady vs steady+burst).

I've attached a preliminary capacity workbook and a short SLA sketch. I'm happy to run a short walkthrough Monday to validate numbers with your infra and procurement.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

Attachments: archimedes_capacity_model.xlsx, SLA-proposal-archimedes.pdf

On a related note, cc'ing Grace and Vivek for ops/architecture sanity checks.

From: Emma Hart <emma.hart@archimedeslabs.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@archimedeslabs.com>, procurement@archimedeslabs.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: throughput & SLA mapping for Dedicated commitment

Alex —

Thanks, this is very helpful. Quick clarifications:

- Our traced cache-hit was 42% on prefixes (I rounded up in my note). So your 45% assumption is fine.
- We prefer to start with FP16 for quality reasons; quantization is acceptable for a lower-cost fallback pool for non-critical workflows.
- For procurement: we want reserved steady capacity with a 2x peak burst option for the first 6 months. Please include pricing for both steady-only and steady+burst in the SOW.
- Our peak hour profile (from uploads): at 220 req/sec peak, average tokens per request in peak rises to 160 (more mid-length).
- We intend to enable prefix caching for ~60% of conversational sessions (customer reuse), but cache hit quality drops on sessions with high dynamic inputs. For modeling please keep the 45% active hit assumption but show sensitivity at 35% and 55%.

Also adding procurement: procurement@archimedeslabs.com is the right contact for SOW & DocuSign. Our target decision gating is a combined: performance fit + price <= budget cap.

Can we set a follow-up call Tuesday 11/24 at 10:00 PT to go through the workbook with Grace/Vivek? Samir will join for Qs on burst routing.

—Emma

Attachment: none

Emma / Samir / procurement team —

Thanks for the confirmation on assumptions. Per our call notes, here's the agreed recommendation and immediate next steps:

Final recommended sizing (narrowed):
- Steady reserved commitment: 6 H200-equivalent slabs (FP16) mapped to an estimated effective compute capacity of ~5.1k tokens/sec with current caching assumptions (45% hit).
- Pricing options: steady-only (6 slabs) and steady+burst (6 steady + 6 dynamic burst slabs). I'll have Ben produce a price delta and show amortized per-token units.
- Headroom/SLAs: 35% steady headroom target; projected P95 server-side latency ~265ms under steady; peak-burst path keeps P95 <= 320ms for long-form but <280ms for short/medium.
- Fallbacks: enable quantized fallback pool (4 slabs quantized) for non-interactive batch workloads; route very long generations (>500 tokens) to a dedicated async tier.

Deliverables I'll share by EOD Wed:
1) Updated capacity workbook with sensitivity columns for 35% / 45% / 55% cache hit rates. (archimedes_capacity_model.xlsx)
2) SLA + SOW draft with steady vs steady+burst pricing and DocuSign-ready version. (SLA-proposal-archimedes.pdf)
3) Quick ops runbook notes for cache warmup and autoscale guardrails.

Action items for Archimedes:
- Procurement: confirm which pricing option you want in the initial quote (steady-only or steady+burst).
- Eng: confirm that FP16 is required for customer-facing flows; if you permit partial quantization for fallback, we can include that in the price delta.

I'll loop in Ben for the pricing numbers and Grace/Vivek for any final architecture signoffs. Proposed follow-up: Thu 11/26 would also work if Tue is a problem.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into the SOW.

Alex Martinez
